38854-the-maid-of-honour-a-tale-of-the-d.creator: Unknown
38854-the-maid-of-honour-a-tale-of-the-d.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. Not the purse exactly, for there existed that hateful allowance, which he would never, never soil his fingers with; but the marital authority and position which go with unstinted means! They had both shrivelled away, and the Marquis de Gange smarted as if he had been tarred and feathered. What would people say when the last whimsey of the chatelaine leaked out?

arxiv-2007-05462.title: Beam Divergence Reduction of Vortex Waves with a Tailored Lens and a Tailored Reflector
arxiv-2007-05462.creator: M. Haj Hassan 1 , B. Sievert 1 , J. T. Svejda 1 , A. Mostafa Ahmad 2 , J. Barowski 3 , A. Rennings 1 , I. Rolfes 3 , A. Sezgin 2 , and D. Erni 1
arxiv-2007-05462.description: Abstract In this paper, we present a tailored lens and a tailored reflector in order to reduce the large beam divergence inherent to Orbital Angular Momentum waves (OAM waves/Vortex waves) that are generated by an Uniform Circular Patch Antenna Array (UCA) at 10 ​ GHz 10\,\mathrm{GHz} .

arxiv-2011-08895.title: ZORB: A Derivative-Free Backpropagation Algorithm for Neural Networks
arxiv-2011-08895.creator: Varun Ranganathan, Alex Lewandowski
arxiv-2011-08895.description: Abstract Gradient descent and backpropagation have enabled neural networks to achieve remarkable results in many real-world applications. Despite ongoing success, training a neural network with gradient descent can be a slow and strenuous affair. We present a simple yet faster training algorithm called Zeroth-Order Relaxed Backpropagation (ZORB). Instead of calculating gradients, ZORB uses the pseudoinverse of targets to backpropagate information.

arxiv-2107-08316.title: Algebraic and analytic compactifications of moduli spaces
arxiv-2107-08316.creator: Patricio Gallardo, Matt Kerr
arxiv-2107-08316.description: Abstract . In this expository note, we offer an overview of the relationship between Hodge-theoretic and geometric compactifications of moduli spaces of algebraic varieties. The tour ahead When studying algebraic objects, like subvarieties of a projective space, one notices that they are defined by polynomials, whose coefficients can vary.

arxiv-2307-00303.title: Efficient Calculation the Number of Partitions of the Set { 1 , 2 , … , 3 ​ n } \{1,2,\ldots,3n\} into Subsets { x , y , z } \{x,y,z\} Satisfying x + y = z x+y=z
arxiv-2307-00303.description: Abstract Consider the set { 1 , 2 , … , 3 ​ n } \{1,2,\ldots,3n\} . We are interested in the number of partitions of this set into subsets of three elements each, where the sum of two of them equals the third.

arxiv-2403-01703.title: Bergman algebras The graded universal algebra constructions
arxiv-2403-01703.creator: R. Hazrat, H. Li, R. Preusser
arxiv-2403-01703.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by R. Hazrat, H. Li, R. Preusser. A half a century ago, George Bergman introduced stunning machinery which would realise any commutative conical monoid as the non-stable K K -theory of a ring. The ring constructed is “minimal” or “universal”.

arxiv-2405-06317.title: Difference “abc” theorem for entire functions and Difference analogue of truncated version of Nevanlinna second main theorem
arxiv-2405-06317.creator: Rui-Chun Chen, Zhi-Tao Wen
arxiv-2405-06317.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Rui-Chun Chen, Zhi-Tao Wen. In this paper, we focus on the difference analogue of the Stothers-Mason theorem for entire functions of order less than 1, which can be seen as difference a ​ b ​ c abc theorem for entire functions.

arxiv-2406-13763.title: Through the Theory of Mind’s Eye: Reading Minds with Multimodal Video Large Language Models
arxiv-2406-13763.creator: Zhawnen Chen, Tianchun Wang, Yizhou Wang, Michal Kosinski, Xiang Zhang, Yun Fu, Sheng Li
arxiv-2406-13763.description: Abstract Can large multimodal models have a human-like ability for emotional and social reasoning, and if so, how does it work? Recent research has discovered emergent theory-of-mind (ToM) reasoning capabilities in large language models (LLMs). LLMs can reason about people’s mental states by solving various text-based ToM tasks that ask questions about the actors’ ToM (e.g., human belief, desire, intention).

arxiv-2503-16342.title: HiQ-Lip: The First Quantum-Classical Hierarchical Method for Global Lipschitz Constant Estimation of ReLU Networks
arxiv-2503-16342.creator: Haoqi He & Yan Xiao
arxiv-2503-16342.description: Abstract Estimating the global Lipschitz constant of neural networks is crucial for understanding and improving their robustness and generalization capabilities. However, precise calculations are NP-hard, and current semidefinite programming (SDP) methods face challenges such as high memory usage and slow processing speeds.

arxiv-2504-19159.title: Spectral form factor of quadratic 𝑹 R -para-particle SYK model with Random Matrix Coupling
arxiv-2504-19159.creator: Tingfei Li
arxiv-2504-19159.description: Abstract This paper investigates the spectral form factor (SFF) of the quadratic R R -para-particle Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev ( R R -PSYK 2 ) model with various random matrix ensemble couplings. We generalize previous work on Gaussian Unitary Ensemble (GUE) couplings to all three Gaussian ensembles (GUE, GOE, GSE) and three circular ensembles (CUE, COE, CSE).

arxiv-2506-05589.title: UTSA-NLP at ArchEHR-QA 2025: Improving EHR Question Answering via Self-Consistency Prompting
arxiv-2506-05589.creator: Sara Shields-Menard, Zach Reimers, Joshua Gardner
arxiv-2506-05589.description: Abstract We describe our system for the ArchEHR-QA Shared Task on answering clinical questions using electronic health records (EHRs). Our approach uses large language models in two steps: first, to find sentences in the EHR relevant to a clinician’s question, and second, to generate a short, citation-supported response based on those sentences.

arxiv-2507-05489.title: Higher-Order Newton-Cartan Gravity
arxiv-2507-05489.creator: Biel Cardona and Luca Romano
arxiv-2507-05489.description: Abstract August 8, 2026 1 Departamento de Electromagnetismo y Electrónica, Universidad de Murcia, Campus de Espinardo, 30100 Murcia, Spain Abstract We study the non-relativistic Newton-Cartan limit of higher-order gravity theories in arbitrary dimensions. We first study it at the level of the action by introducing an additional 1-form gauge field and coupling it appropriately to the gravity sector.

arxiv-2507-15945.title: Extracting Essential Non-perturbative Information in Jet Invariant Mass via the Bayesian Analysis
arxiv-2507-15945.creator: Zhan Gao, Yu Shi, Bo-Wen Xiao, Han-Zhong Zhang
arxiv-2507-15945.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Zhan Gao, Yu Shi, Bo-Wen Xiao, Han-Zhong Zhang. In this paper, we present a new three-dimensional non-perturbative (NP) function to account for and parameterize the NP contributions in the jet invariant mass spectrum, in addition to the conventional NP mass shift parametrization.

arxiv-2509-11451.title: Maui : Reconstructing Private Client Data in Federated Transfer Learning
arxiv-2509-11451.creator: Ahaan Dabholkar, Atul Sharma, Z. Berkay Celik, Saurabh Bagchi, {adabholk, sharm438, zcelik, sbagchi}@purdue.edu
arxiv-2509-11451.description: Abstract Recent works in federated learning (FL) have shown the utility of leveraging transfer learning for balancing the benefits of FL and centralized learning. In this setting, federated training happens after a stable point has been reached through conventional training.

pmc-10582333.title: YIV-818-A: a novel therapeutic agent in prostate cancer management through androgen receptor downregulation, glucocorticoid receptor inhibition, epigenetic regulation, and enhancement of apalutamide, darolutamide, and enzalutamide efficacy
pmc-10582333.creator: Wing Lam, Mohammad Arammash, Wei Cai, Fulan Guan, Zaoli Jiang, Shwu-Huey Liu, Peikwen Cheng, Yung-Chi Cheng
pmc-10582333.description: Introduction: Prostate cancer is the second leading cause of cancer death among men in the United States. Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer (CRPC) often develops resistance to androgen deprivation therapy. Resistance in CRPC is often driven by AR variants and glucocorticoid receptor (GR). Thus, drugs that target both could be vital in overcoming resistance.

pmc-11446847.title: Connectomic reconstruction predicts visual features used for navigation
pmc-11446847.creator: Dustin Garner, Emil Kind, Jennifer Yuet Ha Lai, Aljoscha Nern, Arthur Zhao, Lucy Houghton, Gizem Sancer, Tanya Wolff, Gerald M. Rubin, Mathias F. Wernet, Sung Soo Kim
pmc-11446847.description: Many animals use visual information to navigate1–4, but how such information is encoded and integrated by the navigation system remains incompletely understood. In Drosophila melanogaster, EPG neurons in the central complex compute the heading direction5 by integrating visual input from ER neurons6–12, which are part of the anterior visual pathway (AVP)10,13–16.

pmc-11579936.title: Functionalization of Nanodiamond Surfaces with Metal β-Diketonato Complexes with Possible Application in Cancer Treatment
pmc-11579936.creator: Siyanda Khoza, Anke Wilhelm, Elizabeth Erasmus, Eleanor Fourie
pmc-11579936.description: Nanodiamonds (NDs) are used more frequently as drug carriers through absorption or chemical modification. In this report, we describe the chemical binding of metal β-diketonato complexes onto the ND surface using an aminosilane linker. The metals used were iron(III) and copper(II), with β-diketones, acetylacetone, trifluoroacetylacetone, and the naturally occurring curcumin, which is known for its biological activity.

pmc-11587780.title: Transcriptomic analysis reveals differential transcriptional regulation underlying Citrus Bacterial Canker (CBC) tolerance in Citrus sinensis
pmc-11587780.creator: Zhigang Ouyang, Xinyou Wang, Xi Peng, Leijian Zhong, Wei Zeng, Tongqi Huang, Ruimin Li
pmc-11587780.description: The sustainable development of the citrus industry is greatly affected by citrus canker, an important bacterial disease. To explore the transcriptional regulatory mechanism of citrus resistance to canker disease, this study used the susceptible Citrus sinensis cv. ‘Newhall’ and its citrus canker-resistant bud mutation variety ‘Longhuitian’ (LHT) as materials.

pmc-11604469.title: How Early Is Early?
pmc-11604469.creator: Peter Calvert
pmc-11604469.description: Corresponding AuthorKey Words: ablation, atrial fibrillation, cryoballoon, early Atrial fibrillation (AF) may cause a variety of symptoms—from palpitations to breathlessness, fatigue to clinical heart failure (HF). The coexistence of AF and HF is not infrequently seen in practice,1 and may significantly worsen both symptoms and prognosis.

pmc-11648115.title: Cholesterol: The driving force behind the remodeling of tumor microenvironment in colorectal cancer
pmc-11648115.creator: Ke Wang, Yuanyuan Zhang, Chengshuai Si, Yuepeng Cao, Peng Shao, Pei Zhang, Nannan Wang, Guoqing Su, Jinghang Qian, Liu Yang
pmc-11648115.description: Essential membrane components and metabolites with a wide range of biological roles are both produced by cholesterol metabolism. Cell-intrinsic and cell-extrinsic stimuli alter cholesterol metabolism in the tumor microenvironment (TME), which in turn encourages colorectal carcinogenesis. Metabolites produced from cholesterol play intricate roles in promoting the development of colorectal cancer (CRC) and stifling immunological responses.

pmc-12838975.title: Gut Microbial Composition and Short-Chain Fatty Acid Metabolism in Cognitively Unimpaired Adults Stratified by Amyloid-β Status
pmc-12838975.creator: D. M. Sithara Dissanayaka, Thilini N. Jayasinghe, Hamid R. Sohrabi, S. R. Rainey-Smith, Kevin Taddei, Colin L. Masters, Ralph N. Martins, W. M. A. D. Binosha Fernando
pmc-12838975.description: Short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) produced by gut microbial fermentation influence host metabolism and neuroinflammatory processes implicated in Alzheimer’s disease (AD). However, the relationship between fecal SCFAs, microbial taxa, and cerebral amyloid-β (Aβ) burden in cognitively unimpaired individuals remains unclear. Fecal SCFAs were quantified using GC-MS, and microbial species were profiled by shotgun metagenomics in 87 participants.

pmc-13009260.title: Empathy for pain in humans and animals differs based on species, psychosocial and cultural factors
pmc-13009260.creator: Maria Suñol, Brock Bastian, Marina López-Solà
pmc-13009260.description: Empathy for others’ pain guides moral concern and prosocial behaviour, yet how it extends across species remains to be elucidated. This study examined how people perceive and respond to pain in humans and animals, and how these responses relate to psychosocial traits.
